detail:
Decisions: Chose Dave's Option A — scope accumulates as a sorted comma-joined set — over first-writer-wins or dropping the property; it is the only option that loses no information, it converges so the entity file stops being rewritten, and it is backward compatible because an existing singular value is a valid one-element set and both consumers do substring matching; Chose to put the merge rule in a shared utils/entity-properties.ts consumed by BOTH graph backends rather than editing each addEntity separately — the file and sqlite stores carried byte-identical `{...existing, ...input}` merges and the sqlite store's header explicitly promises upsert parity, so duplicating the special case would have been a future divergence; Chose to sort the accumulated set rather than preserve insertion order — ordering alone would otherwise churn the committed entity JSON, and a deterministic order makes the cap stable so a capped entity converges instead of oscillating; Chose to cap the set at 12 entries / 480 chars, dropping in sort order — tool schema caps property values at 1000 chars and a central file in a 2,300-decision project can be touched from many scopes; dropping in sort order is arbitrary but stable, whereas dropping oldest would reintroduce the churn the fix exists to remove; Chose to make the repair pass union the recovered scopes with the stored value rather than replace it — a stored scope with no decided_by edge backing it (hand-written via twining_add_entity) is still a real observation, so replacement would destroy data the overwrite bug never touched; Chose to widen GraphEngine.graphStore from private to readonly-public rather than add delegate methods for getEntities/getRelations — the repair pass needs to walk the whole graph once, and growing the engine a method per query shape to preserve nominal encapsulation is worse than exposing the store it already wraps
Findings: Repair verified against the real dogfood store in preview mode: 677 entities examined, 101 repairable, nothing written. Concrete recovery: src/storage/decision-store.ts was stamped scope 'src/engine/' (contradicting its own path) and recovers 'src/,src/engine/,src/engine/decisions.ts,src/storage/' — including the correct src/storage/. src/server.ts recovers 9 scopes from a stored 'project'.; The repair has NOT been executed on this repo — it would rewrite 101 committed entity records, which is the owner's call. Run twining_housekeeping({repair_entity_scopes: true}) to preview, add execute: true to apply.; warning: the cap drops scopes in sort order, so an entity touched from more than 12 scopes will silently lose the alphabetically-later ones. Stable and convergent by design, but it means a very hot file's scope set is a subset, not the truth. If that matters, the alternative is raising the cap or moving scope off file entities entirely (Option B).; Test note: my first convergence test did not discriminate — under last-writer-wins, writing a/,b/,a/,b/ ends at b/ either way. Rewrote it to write a/,b/ then a/ AGAIN, which flips the value back under the old semantics and is a no-op under a union. Three of the eight tests now fail against unfixed code.
summary: Implemented Option A: graph entity scope now accumulates as a sorted set, with an opt-in repair pass for the 101 already-overwritten entities
